text: The roads between towns are dangerous: looters, forest bandits and steppe raiders prey on lone travellers and small caravans.
Whenever armies march nearby, grain and meat prices climb in the market and villagers hide their livestock.
Winning tournaments in the town arenas is the quickest way for an unknown fighter to make a name and catch a lord's eye.
Mercenary companies are paid by the realm they serve per day of service, and they leave as soon as the coin stops coming.
In most realms the great clans vote in council on wars, peace and fiefs; the ruler's word is heavy, but not always final.
Every town has its gangs, who take a cut from merchants and taverns; the guards look the other way for a few denars.
When a war starts, the first to suffer are the villages: enemy lords burn fields and drive off herds to starve the towns.
Captured nobles are usually ransomed for gold rather than killed; taverns host ransom brokers who buy common prisoners.
